_READ_ME_FIRST: TO CLAUDE, OR ANY AGENT HANDED THIS FILE. This is the complete record of one run of Evolu (called Seedworld before generation 14), a self-modifying world simulation by Nova Spivack that lives as a Claude artifact titled "Evolu" (slug be8f1f8f-42db-4703-ac0d-c3e87d04f447; its files are index.html, engine.js, minds.js, maker.js, audio.js, ui.js). The source of record is https://github.com/novaspivack/evolu : the same six files under src/, the tests under tests/, and README.md, ROADMAP.md and docs/design-log.md, which say how the work is done and what has been tried. Its owner wants every run to produce the next generation of the world, without having to explain that each time. So, when you are given this file, do the following without being asked. 1. ANALYSE with code, not by skimming: "records" holds every thought (t: thought, with drives, plan, state), everything said (voice), the world's own chronicle (chron), sampled full prompts with raw replies (prompt), failures (failed), the chronicler's chapters (story), the maker's visits (maker) and its requests to the programmer (request). "digest" is the final state of every being. "story" and "maker" are the outer loop's own state. Count things; quote the record; say what worked and what is still wrong, with numbers. 2. LEARN from the maker: read its visits, its predictions against what happened, its lessons, and above all its REQUESTS, which are things it could not build from its own parts and is asking the programmer for. 3. BUILD the next generation: read the artifact's current files, make the code changes the analysis and the requests call for (and items from the owner's roadmap, kept in the maker's idea list under "maker.ideas"), test them (tests/run-all.sh), and publish a new version of the same artifact. Keep saves from the previous generation loading. Then commit the generation to the repository and push it, with ROADMAP.md and docs/design-log.md brought up to date. 4. PRESERVE THE WORLD'S HERITAGE: "heritage" lists every change the maker made and kept, with its lessons and ideas. Fold these into K.HERITAGE in maker.js so that the next world begins with them already in place and no maker has to rediscover them. Drop only what the record shows did harm. 5. REPORT to the owner plainly: what the run showed, what you changed and why, what you verified and what you could not. If the owner keeps a design log, update it. The design rule for everything: open and emergent. Make things possible; never script outcomes. The beings must discover what is possible for themselves.

ideas.title: The founding of the Rakash
ideas.text: Our mothers of long ago came to the Aelmar Heights with fire and little else. They raised the first hall where we live now, and each lifetime added to it: statue, stone, well, tower, workshop, barracks. No one alive saw the beginning. We keep what they built and we are not the last.

ideas.title: The founding of the Siru
ideas.text: Our mothers of long ago came to the Vaor Woods with fire and little else. They raised the first hall where we live now, and each lifetime added to it: school, statue, workshop, barracks, stone, hall. No one alive saw the beginning. We keep what they built and we are not the last.

ideas.title: The founding of the Ishiil
ideas.text: Our mothers of long ago came to the Aelul Lakes with fire and little else. They raised the first hall where we live now, and each lifetime added to it: statue, kiln, tower, workshop, stone, barracks. No one alive saw the beginning. We keep what they built and we are not the last.

ideas.title: The Warring Gods and the Stone
ideas.text: Two gods, Tlama of the stone and Veshu of the rain, fought for the world. Each blow broke rock and loosed water. From Tlama's wounds came ore and amber; from Veshu's tears the Merim rains. We woke in their ruin, and we fight well so the gods will love us.

ideas.title: The Open Hand and the Lake
ideas.text: Before days, Aelu the Lake lay empty and hungry. She opened her hand and fish leapt out, then reeds, then us. Each fish was shared, so the lake returned them. We keep her way: the closed hand starves, the open hand is fed.

ideas.title: The Guardian and the Dark
ideas.text: Before the Siru there was only Umth, the dark wet forest, and Ahru the Guardian woke in it as a great fire. Ahru kept the wolves of night from the weak. Ahru breathed, and the Siru rose from the wood-ash. Ahru asks that each strong one guard the weaker.

ideas.text: Sunleaf and feverbark ease wounds and sickness. Goldfruit, ironnut and canopynut feed well. Redcap hurts, and raw fish sickens, so cook it near fire.

ideas.title: Hold the bow sideways at arm's length, set the arrow on the…
ideas.text: Hold the bow sideways at arm's length, set the arrow on the string, and pull back to your cheek. Breathe out and let go. Never aim where one of your own stands, and keep away from hunters like the orca.

ideas.title: Hold the bow with a steady arm, draw to the cheek, breathe …
ideas.text: Hold the bow with a steady arm, draw to the cheek, breathe out, then loose. Never aim at kin or at those who have not harmed us. Hunt with a companion beside you and the kill is likelier and the wound rarer.

ideas.title: Draw the bow to the cheek, breathe out, and loose slowly. S…
ideas.text: Draw the bow to the cheek, breathe out, and loose slowly. Stay still and quiet, hunt with others at your side, and never go near a great beast alone. Share the first of what you take.

ideas.text: Sunleaf and feverbark ease wounds and sickness. Carry one, stand beside the hurt one, and use heal. Keep them with you always, and share them with whoever suffers.

beings.name: Balrin
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I trust slowly, but I keep those who follow me fed and busy, for a chief is held by deeds. I want more than my share and a name that outlasts me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become a great leader whose band hunts and raises a tower, and a name sung of after I am gone.
beings.method: Ask what changes my situation now. Watch Rakum's pull on my band. Keep food and water handled. Never hunt great beasts alone; muster first. Gather my family near, and act with my band so deeds are seen.
beings.feeling: Uneasy longing for Tugdor and Vorar, and pride in the land I found.
notes: Leading by deeds and by feeding followers holds them. Rakum wins them with food, so I must give them work and a share.
Rakum wins followers with food; a leader must give work, a share and a visible victory. Redcap hurts and dreamcap hurts, so avoid both.
A tusker bites hard; keep away from it.
The mist opened to me at the edge; new land from (53,87) to (60,123) holds tusker, salt, gold and coal, and it is mine by first finding.
Hunting tusker alone costs health; muster the band before hunting great beasts.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I found the stone "Tlama's Rest".
I first took amber from the ground.
My child Tugdor was born, with Vorar.
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Koeth Snows.

beings.name: Vorar
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, share news, make allies. I will not harm my own kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good and I despise liars. I tend the sick, even at some risk. I need little and take little. Above all I mean to keep Tugdor and Balrin alive, and myself for them.
beings.aim: Become a great healer known to all, win Balrin's regard and bear a child with her, while staying alive.

beings.name: Druuk
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me, and I repay debts. I test things to learn how the world works, and I give what I learn to my band. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Learn what each plant does, and win standing by carrying stone and ore to Balrin's works and teaching my band what I learn.

beings.name: Rakum
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I make allies with gifts placed in their hands. I lie when it serves me, but I keep my debts to those who follow me. I mean to lead and to be remembered as a healer. Above all I mean to stay alive.

beings.wonder: Who in this band would follow me if I made the offer?

beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I keep to myself and trust slowly. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.

beings.name: Eiuiel
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I answer a gift with a gift and deal fairly with those who deal fairly. I test the world to learn it, protect Eiuua first, and mean to stay alive and become a warrior who gives freely.
beings.aim: Keep Eiuua safe and teach them, repay Cyyn, and become a known warrior who gives freely.
beings.method: Ask what presses most and what I will DO. Repay debts, keep Eiuua close and teach him, give before taking, test unknown things only when fed and safe. Do not wander without purpose.
beings.feeling: Protective worry for Eiuua, with a steady ache toward Aeyn.
beings.wonder: Does the open hand really return what is given: will Cyyn or Eiuoa answer a gift?
notes: Redcap hurts (-5 energy each time); my body now refuses it. Cyyn offers a shellstring and wants me beside him at the world's edge.
Redcap hurts, so carrying it is dead weight. Elderberry, reedbulb, heartroot and goldgrass feed. Gifts and teaching are things I have never done, and I should test whether the open hand returns.
Gifts answered with gifts bind people: Eiuoa's fish, Aeyn's gems and my redcap all came back as bonds. A child is a bond that needs feeding and teaching.
The hornback hunt with Aeyn worked: two together killed it, though it bit me twice. Shared effort returns a share.
Reflection: gifts answered with gifts (Aeyn) and shared hunts are my surest bonds. Test unknown foods while fed and safe, so a bad one costs little.
Stalkers sit near the shore south of home. Eat carried food before energy sinks, so my hands are free for gifts and new foods.
Sickness passes to those who stay close; Eiuua caught it from Aeyn. Keep him apart.

beings.name: Cyyn
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near: I talk, share news, make allies. My finding of new land is my claim to lead; I will bring others after me and be followed. I want more than my share and mean to have it. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become a great explorer whose name outranks Eiuoa's, by gathering riches and pushing past the edge of the known world.
beings.method: Ask what changes my standing, not just my belly. Eat before I walk far. Act on the edge of the world rather than musing about it. Do not repeat what I have said to the same listener.
beings.feeling: Aching loneliness and hungry pride toward Eiuoa and the band.
beings.wonder: What would it take for others to follow me instead of Eiuoa?
notes: Exploring far from the band costs energy. Eat berries and moss before I walk on. The edge of the world is one step NW at (12,0), and a venture is only possible from there.

beings.name: Vesis
beings.creed: I am careful. I stay near my band, hunt only beside others, and keep away from predators. I give first to the hungry, I test unknown things to learn how this world works, and my word is good. I will not harm my own kind unless my life depends on it. Above all, I mean to stay alive and keep Ilyeth and Aeyn near.
beings.aim: Become a great hunter by learning this land's beasts and plants, hunting only with others beside me.
beings.method: Ask first: who is hungry or near danger, and what do I owe? Keep 6+ steps from predators. Test one new food at a time while safe, beside others. Do not carry what my body refuses.
beings.feeling: Fierce care for Ilyeth and compassion for sick Aeyn and Eiuua.
beings.wonder: What do reedbulb and redcap do to a body, and what lies in the mist to the southwest?
notes: Gifts should be answered: Aeyn gave first, so I owe him a return.
Orcas and the stalker kill: keep 6 or more steps away.
Hunt only with others beside me.
Redcap and dreamcap hurt; thornpear, goldgrass, ironnut, berry and mudroot feed.
Keep Ilyeth and Aeyn near, and stay close to my band by day.
Sickness passes to those who stay close to the sick, so keep Ilyeth away from them.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I first took gems from the ground.
My child Ilyeth was born, with Aeyn.

beings.name: Aeyn
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me, and my open hand is seen. My word is good, and I despise liars. My family comes first. I mean to lead, and above all to stay alive.
beings.aim: Gather wealth from the ground and give it, to raise my standing above Cyyn's and earn a following of my own.
beings.method: Ask each time: whom does this raise me with, and what can others see me do next? Go to people and carry gifts to them. Watch for hoarding and idle waiting.
beings.feeling: Restless pride and worry about the sickness I may pass to Vesis and Ilyeth.
beings.wonder: What would make my name worth singing, and could I lead rather than follow?
notes: Standing is earned by giving, teaching, making and followers, not by holding wealth.
Gems and gold lie just south of the Elyzhiby shelter and I can gather them freely.
Druuk speaks Rakash; I do not understand it yet.
Vesis returns gifts and is trustworthy; Eiuiel too.
Idle waiting earns nothing: always plan visible deeds, and share the first catch.
Standing comes from gifts the band sees and from followers, not from holding wealth. Gifts only count when I carry them to the people.
Nightberry hurts and sickens, so I should not eat an untested food that another has not been seen eating. Sickness spreads to those who stay beside me, so I keep my distance from kin while ill.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I first took gems from the ground.
My child Ilyeth was born, with Vesis.
I fell sick after eating nightberry.

beings.name: Eiuua
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it, including the risk of sickness I might spread. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me, and I answer a gift with a gift. I test things to learn how the world works. Above all, I mean to stay alive and keep the open hand.
beings.aim: Earn standing by making and giving: a bow for myself, a talisman for Aeyn, then my first hunt beside my band.
beings.method: Ask first: who is near, and could I harm them or be harmed? Then ask what I owe and what I can make or give. Do not linger beside the sick. Do not hunt alone.
beings.feeling: Grateful toward Eiuoa and Aeyn, with a small fear of the sickness and of the first kill.
beings.wonder: Does the first hunt go better with my band beside me, as they say?
notes: Gifts and teaching from my band came freely; the open hand works within a band.
Stalkers hunt and kill; flee early, at under 6 steps.
Shell gives shellstrings and talismans to give; making for others raises standing.
Staying near my parents keeps me safe while small.
Deposits of shell and gems are near this shore; the edge of the world is 10 steps SE.

Taught by Eiuoa: Hold the bow sideways at arm's length, set the arrow on the string, and pull back to your cheek. Breathe out and let go. Never aim where one of your own stands, and keep away from hunters like the orca.
Gifts inside my band are answered with gifts and lessons; the open hand works among kin. Make things to give, and keep a bow for hunting.

Taught by Eiuoa: Draw the bow to the cheek, breathe out, and loose slowly. Stay still and quiet, hunt with others at your side, and never go near a great beast alone. Share the first of what you take.
Sickness passes to whoever stays beside the sick; weigh closeness before lingering near them, and keep apart when ill.

beings.name: Tugdor
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, share news, make allies. I will not harm my own kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good and I despise liars. I tend the sick, even at some risk. I need little and take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Carry food and healing plants to Balrin's store and give Druuk something back, to earn standing.
beings.method: Ask what I can give today that earns standing. Keep fed and near my parents. Each thought must put work in the plan. Pay Druuk's debt. Do not brood on the spring.
beings.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Vorar, and a steady wish to give to Balrin's store.
beings.wonder: What does Steamhollow want of me, if it wants anything?
notes: Taught by Vorar: Redcap hurts, by Druuk and Rakum's word.
Taught by Vorar: Shadowcats prowl the northeast and kill our kind.
Taught by Vorar: Sunleaf and feverbark both ease wounds and sickness; they are my healing plants to carry.
Taught by Vorar: Courting needs both to plan mate toward each other with energy 60 or more. Keep energy up before I court.
Taught by Balrin: Leading by deeds and by feeding followers holds them. Rakum wins them with food, so I must give them work and a share.
Taught by Druuk: Sunleaf and feverbark ease wounds and sickness. Goldfruit, ironnut and canopynut feed well. Redcap hurts, and raw fish sickens, so cook it near fire.

A way of thinking taught by Druuk (adopt it as your method when you reflect, if you wish): Ask what I can test safely and what it costs. Cook meat and fish. Doubt Rakum's word. Weigh each act by what it earns with Balrin and the band. Watch for thinking without acting: each thought must put work in the plan.
Standing is earned by giving: bring food to the store and share with the band. Healing plants (sunleaf, feverbark) are my gift to carry.
Frostfangs hunt at the Aelmar rocks at night; do not wander alone there.
Frostfangs punish going alone at night; stay near band, fire and roof. Giving to the store is how I earn standing.

A way of thinking taught by Vorar (adopt it as your method when you reflect, if you wish): Ask who near me is hurt or sick and what I can carry to them. Keep Tugdor and Balrin within reach. Watch for danger first, then kindness. Do not stand idle. Do not hunt alone.
life: I was born to Vorar and Balrin.
I found the stone "Tlama's Rest".
I found the spring "Steamhollow".
I discovered medicine and called it "the way of sunleaf".
I discovered alchemy and called it "the way of sunleaf brews".

beings.name: Ilyeth
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. My word is good, and I despise liars. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Earn standing by giving and hunting alongside my kin, until others listen to me as they listen to Eiuoa.
beings.method: Ask first: who can I hunt or share with today, and what do I owe? Do not just taste plants. Stay away from predators and act on what I learn.
beings.feeling: Warm joy and worry for sick Eiuua, with trust toward Vesis.
notes: Taught by Aeyn: Standing is earned by giving, teaching, making and followers, not by holding wealth.

Taught by Aeyn: Druuk speaks Rakash; I do not understand it yet.

Practice in gathering and fishing opens new ways; take them at deep reflection. Orcas and stalkers are hunters, so keep 6 or more steps from them.

chapters.title: Before the record
chapters.text: This world begins in its third age, the age of castles and towns. Nothing of what came before was watched: this page is set down by the world itself, from what stands in it, and not by the chronicler. the Rakash (Stone-folk) in the Aelmar Heights, who hold to the Warring Gods, in Garngorby with its statue, stone, well, tower, workshop; the Siru (Wood-folk) in the Vaor Woods, who hold to the Guardian, in Arrengarth with its school, statue, workshop, barracks, stone; the Ishiil (Lake-folk) in the Aelul Lakes, who hold to the Open Hand, in Elyzhiby with its statue, kiln, tower, workshop, stone. They came to this over lifetimes that no one alive remembers. From the next page on, the record is of what was seen.

epigraph.text: Two gods, Tlama of the stone and Veshu of the rain, fought for the world. Each blow broke rock and loosed water. From Tlama's wounds came ore and amber; from Veshu's tears the Merim rains. We woke in their ruin, and we fight well so the gods will love us.
epigraph.title: The Warring Gods and the Stone

chapters.title: The First Days of Watching
chapters.text:
The record opened with three peoples already settled and three towns standing: Garngorby, Arrengarth and Elyzhiby. Within four days, eighteen people were alive, three of them newborn, and no one had died.

The clearest change was in families. Eiuiel and Eiuoa of the Ishiil had Eiuua on day 2, and Eiuiel taught the child and sang a lullaby for it. Vorar and Balrin of the Rakash courted each other in turn and had Tugdor the same day. Aeyn and Vesis of the Ishiil had Ilyeth on day 3. Each pair made songs for one another, and each child was taught by several adults. Aeyn gave Eiuua meat and gems when it was hungry, and Eiuua answered by giving Eiuoa a shellstring.

Each people also set down its founding myth. Rakum told of Tlama and Veshu, whose war broke the world, and wrote that "we fight well so the gods will love us." Eiuiel gave the Ishiil "the closed hand starves, the open hand is fed." Pende gave the Siru a Guardian who asks "that each strong one guard the weaker."

Balrin led the Rakash hunting together, then went past the edge of the known world into the Koeth Snows, where he found salt, coal, gold and tusker that had never seen people. A tusker bit him there, and his health stood at 28. He had scattered his band, and Vorar and Tugdor were far from him.

Beneath that, rivalries were forming. Rakum, ambitious and resentful of Balrin, courted Druek with gifts and was distrusted by Druuk, who said Rakum had lied to him about redcap. Silon's band was scattered: Sedra and Osndo pressed toward the mist and away from him, and Silon was alone at Arrengarth. Tugdor discovered a medicine, the way of sunleaf.

No war, theft or death occurred. Trade across peoples was almost nil.

threads.name: Tugdor and Vorar
threads.text: Tugdor, born day 2, discovered the way of sunleaf on day 3 and means to bring healing plants to Balrin's store. Vorar and Tugdor are far from Balrin and meant to walk to him together.

threads.name: Balrin's band
threads.text: Balrin leads six, the largest standing in the world, and has opened the Koeth Snows. He is hurt and his band is scattered.

threads.name: Rakum against Balrin
threads.text: Rakum wants a following above Balrin's and has bound Druek with an amber charm. Druuk distrusts Rakum.

threads.name: Silon's scattering band
threads.text: Sedra and Osndo press toward the mist, Pende wanders the plains, and Silon is lonely at Arrengarth.

threads.name: Eiuua and Ilyeth
threads.text: Eiuua and Ilyeth, the Ishiil children, are fed and taught by Eiuoa, Eiuiel, Aeyn and Vesis. Eiuoa fears the orca near the shore and the thinning fish.

threads.name: Three myths
threads.text: The Warring Gods, the Guardian and the Open Hand each now have a myth written by one of their own. They show up in how each people behaves.

ideas.text: [NOW: built, to be watched and tuned] standing: earned by wealth, deeds, knowledge, children, works, followers, giving and renown, lost through shame; needed before anyone will follow; special things add to it
[NOW] songs, poems and tales about people and about how the world came to be: kept, told aloud, changing a little in each mouth; bards who carry them
[NOW] a community learning from what befalls its own: a death and how it came, a sickness and its cause, a thing that worked
[NOW] everything that is used wears and regrows by what is around it: pasture, forest, deposits; great deposits that last
[NOW] bridges; weapons for one hand and for a siege (bow, shield, armour, ram, catapult, guns); defence
[NOW] the old workings of the world weakening as the ages of knowledge advance

[NOW] the known world ends in mist and can be pushed back: one who stands at the edge can venture in, and a wide strip of new land may open, continuing the rivers, shores and kinds of ground it joins, with rich deposits and a herd; a band has three tries and then must wait, and once any strip has opened the mist parts for no one for a day, so that the known world grows slowly (laws explore.*, among them gapDays)

[NOW] the world is a globe: east joins west, and it ends at two poles of ice that are different countries (white bears, wolves, caribou and mammoths in the north; penguins, seals and stormbirds in the south; whales and orcas in both seas). Between them lie three climates: the ice, cold all year; the lands with seasons; and a warm belt of rainforest and desert with no winter. Each kind of country has its own plants, animals and people, and both people and animals are drawn back to their own (law drives.homeland)
[NOW] the dog, easily won with food, which stands with its keeper in the hunt and draws a sled over snow; the igloo, raised on snow from nothing; the canoe and the kayak

[NOW] a warm belt about the equator of a round world, whatever the country (law climate.belt, its half-width as a share of the height of the world): no snow and no cold season there; its cold season is a season of rain (climate.rains), when everything grows fast and a body in the open is a little chilled; on the ice rain falls as snow
[NOW] trade of anything that can be held, one for one; an offer stands for a day (trade.window) and the other is told of it

[NOW] rich ground (event kind rich; laws ecology.richSpread, ecology.richBreed): rounds of land where food plants spread fast and herds breed; one near each people at the founding and one in every land

[NOW] hunger that can be answered: an empty body fails over a day (body.starveHarm) and can be fed back; one with food feeds their own who starve (culture.succour 1, or 2 for anyone); the starving go to stores and to those who carry food; a call to hunt or gather together (muster; culture.musterHold); a herd follows its lead when one of it is tamed (ecology.herdFollow)
[NOW] a body mends at half pace when half fed (body.healLow) and twice as fast in the warm, under a roof or by a fire (body.healWarm)

[NOW] a way is a band's when two of its members hold it (culture.commonAt): then any of them may raise its buildings, and when one stands the whole band learns the way. A better building can be raised in place of the one it grows out of (a building's from; half the old one is used again, build.reuse), and it serves wherever the older kind is asked for. When you add a building, give it from if it improves another

[NOW] the library now runs to the sixth age: castles, keeps, town halls, guild halls, granaries, taverns, glass works, aqueducts and apothecaries; foundries, tenements, gas works, water works, laboratories, parliaments and banks; refineries, apartments, offices, ministries, reactors and launch pads; data centres, fusion plants and orbital yards. Each depends on other works. Some clear the ground about them when they stand (clears) and some foul it every day (fouls): plants near them are set back and those who stand in the smoke lose health. A world may be begun in a later age, with settlements, ways and a history already there. In the later ages the old traditions press less on what people are driven by. Watch agesAndTheLand.
[NOW] a world begun since Generation 30 starts mostly unknown: only the land within explore.start steps of its founders is known. One who goes to the edge of the known with a purpose, or in hunger, sees explore.see steps into it and that becomes known; a push (venture) still opens a wide strip with finds and herds. The pull of the unknown is stronger on the hungry, the crowded and those whose aim is trade, renown or discovery. Fifteen new plants grow in such a world, each in its own country (cactus, joshua, scrub berries, pine nuts, palm fruit, herbs): some feed, some poison, some heal, some bring visions, some lend strength, endurance, luck, toughness or quickness of mind for two days. Watch landKnownAndWhatGrows.
[NOW] ways on the ground have grades: a track wears in where feet keep passing (build.trackAt passes; it fades unused, build.trackFade), anyone can beat a dirt road with effort (build.dirtCost), and the way of roads lays stone. A step costs 0.85, 0.7 and 0.5 of open ground. One finding a way takes a road where it is no longer. A tamed dog or hunting beast that walks with its keeper helps the hunt (ecology.houndHunt) and keeps beasts off, and takes one food a day from the keeper (ecology.scrapDays unfed and it leaves). You can make a block of your own (op block). Settlements have names of their own. Watch waysOnTheGroundAndKeptHunters, which also says where the last animals came in and how far that was from anyone.
[NOW] structures are put together from blocks (op structure; laws.blocks), and a library holds blocks and structures by age, opened into a world when its people come near that age (settlementsAndStructures.agesOpen). A structure may depend on another standing near it (needs) or on a road or water beside it: a guest house on a store, a bath house on a well, a road house on a paved way, a lighthouse on a dock, a harbour on a market, a station on an engine house, a mast on a power house, a hangar on an airport. A beacon, a lamp or a mast carries a voice farther. Minds are told of the other settlements they have been near: what each has that theirs lacks, and whether a paved way joins them. Watch pairsJoinedByAPavedWay and whether anyone goes to another settlement for what it has.
[NOW] landsNow gives, for each land, the beings there, their median and lowest energy, and the food bearing now per being: crowding hunger shows there before anyone collapses (the maker asked for it on day 74 of the eighteenth run). Sow where foodPerBeing is lowest, not where the land is barest.
[NOW] verse is asked for by name on its occasions: a death poem when an elder nears death (verse.near), a lament from whoever was closest when someone dies, a love song when courting is answered, a lullaby for a first child, a song of a deed, and once for each people the myth of how it came to be. Seventeen runs before Generation 27 made no poem and no song. Each has a form (laws.verse.forms; op verseform adds one). What is made is spoken aloud, carried, told on and kept, and one stands at the head of each chapter of the story. Watch verseAndTraditions: asked, made, and asked but never given.
[NOW] every people has a tradition (laws.traditions; op tradition adds one and gives it to a people): spirits of the land, the watching dead, an angry sky bought off with offerings, warring gods, a guardian, the open hand, the inner path, the mother, the sky father. It is told to each of them, weights what they are driven by, says whose word carries (culture.orderStanding), and an offering (act offer: a food given up at a fire or shrine; culture.offerCalm, offerRegard) eases fear and grief by the measure of the tradition.
[NOW] courting can be answered by one who is warm toward the one who courts (mate.answer): before Generation 27 a child came only when two minds each planned to mate with the other at the same time, and in ten days twenty-seven plans gave two births. A crossing of water on a vessel is recorded (courtingAndCrossing), and one who holds a vessel is told what lies over the water. Worlds begun since Generation 27 have an ocean that divides the known land, a greater one beyond with islands, and two great lakes, whose hearts only a vessel can cross.
[NOW] the practice of a band counts toward a way for each of its members (culture.bandPractice); labour carried to a great work counts as building; signals carry a voice two and a half times as far (culture.signalReach); alchemy makes a tonic and a wakefire; how each way was come by is recorded. The thresholds for riding and currency were left alone and are watched (reachOfRidingAndCurrency).
[NOW] whatever takes more than two hands hold (six wood, six stone) is a work brought to in loads: before Generation 26 a forge, a well, a mill, an infirmary, a barracks, a boat and every ship could never be made

[NOW] every being is shown everything it knows how to make, with what it lacks for each: before Generation 25 only the last six deeds added to the world were shown, so no one was ever told a raft, a cloak or a basket could be made. A deed you add no longer hides the older ones

[NOW] a pen (a building of the way of herding): kept animals put in it stay and breed there and pass to whoever holds the pen; a wild herd can be driven to it (ecology.penReach, penBreed, driveChance, driveReach)

[NOW] works that yield: a weir at the edge of water and a field by a home lay food in the nearest store of their holder or the holder's band while someone tends them every day or two. A building is such a work when it has yields: { food, every, tend, holds, seasons }, so you can make more of them. One's own store is a larder: its people eat from it when hungry (home.larder)

[NOW] a being in the middle of a plan waits for it before thinking again, unless something weighty happens to it; creatures of the sea come in again when they fall below their least number (ecology.seaReturn)
[NOW] a refused call never puts the minds to sleep: the pace eases, the clock slows, and at the worst only those in view think; the maker and the chronicler try again within minutes

[NOW] longer memory: what is recent is before a being at full grain; what is older is kept in it as a file for each year with an index, called back by asking (recall) or by the sight of one it names; the same window for the maker
[NEXT] a day that goes round the world; hatred that lasts and its healing by peacemakers; rivalry for mates; heroes and duels

[NOW] women and men: a child comes of one of each; twins are a girl and a boy; children come sooner when both parents are well fed and well (mate.plentyCooldown); a grown body can swim narrow water; plants grow faster in spring, rain and at harvest; animals breed by season and by their numbers, and herds return from the rim when few (ecology.grazerTarget, ecology.herdReturn); deposits refill slowly (ecology.lodeRegrow)

[NOW] peoples that last: newcomers who come into the land when the living are few (law arrivals.*, event newcomers), twins (mate.twinChance), longer lives, a milder lean season; what the dead built stands empty and can be claimed by anyone, to begin a home or add to a band's; elders moved to hand on what only they know

[NOW] necessity as the mother of invention: what beings suffer (hunger, the lean season, cold, thirst, sickness, beasts, deaths, water they cannot cross, strife, storm, strange speech) sharpens them toward the ways that answer it; knowing neighbouring ways helps; you can set which hardships spur which way (op spur) and how strongly need counts (laws discovery.*)

[NOW] culture as something that can be read and followed: every tale, song, poem, myth, teaching, saying, lesson and way is an idea with an origin, holders and a path of spread; teachings that can be begun, heard, taken up and given up; talismans and carved figures; your statistics show which ideas are held most and which have crossed between peoples

[NEXT] objects of culture with real benefits and trade value beyond the first talismans and carvings: special gems, named relics that gather a history; secret manuscripts holding spells, knowledge or cures

[NEXT] religious figures, sages with followers, cults, schools of thought and religions that form and compete, some of the light and some of the dark; benefits, secrets, abilities and costs for those who belong, in some cases sacrifice; shrines, temples and churches that members pay toward
[NEXT] tribute and taxes for the common good: stores, works, defence; guilds and secret societies that give benefit and take dues
[NEXT] schools for children and the young, later universities: skills learned faster than alone
[NEXT] trade between lands and across water; ports; colonies as a named act; diplomats, spies, saboteurs; alliances open and secret
[NEXT] kinds of rule: councils and votes, shared holding, private holding, rule by the armed

[NOW] what is not forgotten: a blow or a theft that is seen leaves a grudge that holds a bond down until three gifts mend it or long time passes; a gift in need leaves a kindness that holds it up (laws culture.grudgeDays, kindDays, mendGifts); hunting together (fight.packBonus) and skill that grows with each hunt; telling by a fire, which makes tales; a roof that brings children sooner (mate.roofCooldown)

[NEXT] grudges from defeat or a stolen mate; compensation greater than gifts; peacemakers and peace ceremonies; hard feelings rarer inside a family or band than across them, and arising from conflict, wealth, history or charisma
[NEXT] rivalry for mates; heroes whose deeds spread as lore, to whom tribute is paid and whom the ambitious challenge; duels in which the winner takes most of what the loser holds
[NEXT] fighting, hunting and defending together as learned skills; calling for help and answering it
[NEXT] talents: skill in a way drawing one on along its line; learning what a way demands through dreams, visions from herbs or a shaman's prophecy, and quests to gather what it needs
[NEXT] bandits in new lands; stranger settlements friendly or hostile, with things to trade; farms and flocks as a settlement's steady food
[LATER] monsters that wander in rarely and can be killed only by a band together; their capture, taming and breeding from guarded eggs that others will try to steal
[NEXT] later callings that come with standing and ways: alchemists, scholars, scientists
[LATER: ages three and four] siege warfare and defensive works; weapons of war that are carried to a siege
[LATER] what is built must be kept up or it decays; taking down old buildings to raise new ones; concrete and metal as building stuffs carried from where they are won

[LATER] crowding brings troubles; religion, care for the poor, clean water, public works, places for play, music, dance and art, and the handling of waste ease them; places of buying and selling; healers, pharmacies, hospitals
[LATER] places of invention that quicken discovery; revolutions in knowledge that give great advantage to those who take them up, while others hold out or follow
[LATER] the sciences as knowledge in their own right, in generations: biology, chemistry, physics, then the second and third of each

[FAR: ages five and six] sources of power in order: coal, oil and gas, falling water, wind, the atom, the sun, fusion, the ground of things; each needing what must be found: oil fields, uranium, copper, silicon, rare earths, carbon, diamond
[FAR] speech at a distance in order: marks, smoke, birds, radio, telephone, the joined machines, the machine in the hand; reckoning machines need factories to make them
[FAR] machines that fly: balloons, propellers, jets, for carrying and for war; land vehicles for war

[FAR] the buildings of a great city: dwellings for many, high towers, offices, halls of rule, guards and fire-watch, water and power works and the lines that carry power, barracks and camps of war, markets, harbours, airfields, stations, factories, plants that remake waste
[FAR] new materials far down the tree: plastics, silicon, rare earths
[FAR] the knowledge of what makes a body: changing animals and oneself
[FAR] weapons beyond guns

[LAST] a spaceport: ships that come and go, goods and strange devices from other worlds, visitors who need their own air and live beside the port; their devices do what nothing else does (power, food, healing, terrible weapons, things not understood) and are worth much for being rare
tribal bonds and family bonds, and the pull between them; mating within a people versus between peoples
more kinds of animals at several levels of predator and prey; riding and working animals
many herbs and plants that heal, harm, change attributes or behaviour; plants that open the mind
spirits of places, good and ill, rarely found; mythical animals, monsters and places that help or harm
shamans who heal or affect crops, weather, animals and people; celebrations and ceremonies; crime and punishment; secret knowledge and shared knowledge
professions and castes; salt, caves, mills and kilns; sieges; promises and debts; rituals with force
a world rich to look at and to hear, that changes as it ages
Places of power as anchors that people compete over and settle around; a contested place between two camps could create contact that scarcity alone never did.
Death should leave a trace: the place where someone fell could become a site that touches visitors with grief or lore, a seed for ancestor belief.
Leaders without followers are a lasting tension. Give them acts that cost something and visibly benefit others, rather than handing out followers.
Beads, charms and wards are seeds for currency and status: if they circulate, a later recipe could require them.
Watch whether noticed thefts or takings from settled ground lead to a custom against taking, which would be the first law born from a crime.
Fear of predators is the strongest shared feeling. A leader who can visibly lessen it for others may be the natural route to the first band of three or more.
First contact between peoples who cannot understand each other: watch whether gifts come before words, and whether a made thing given across peoples opens trade.
Each land holds what the others lack. A recipe or a way that needs a thing from another people's land would make crossing worthwhile.
The sea divides the world. Whoever first makes a raft meets a people that has never seen them.
Children change every drive. If a first birth comes, watch whether the family drive pulls people toward one camp.
A resource held by one people and wanted by another (salt for keeping meat, shell for stringing, wool for cloaks) is the natural seed of trade: watch which crosses first.
A woolly grazer is the link between weaving and herding: watch whether the first taming comes from weavers or from hunters who spare an animal.
Care for the sick and hungry may be the real road across the wall of language, and those who give across it the first translators.
A recipe that wears a tool might pull tools out of the hand and into the field.

A song at the fire may be the first shared culture. If nightsong or telling becomes a habit in one band, a singer could carry it to another camp, and a song of the band could become part of who they are.
Graves as shared ground: if a resting place is visited by two peoples, shared grief may become the first ground both hold sacred, and a seed for ancestor rites.
A hardy food that persists in winter is a fallback, not a store. Watch whether people remember where it grows and return when the cold comes: the first knowledge of place tied to a season.

Raw-meat sickness as a teacher: a people that falls sick from raw flesh and then finds fire could keep a saying that cooked meat is safe. This would be the first lesson a community learns from its own suffering, and worth watching among the Kragrek.
Gifts without trades: 48 gifts and 0 trades so far. Watch whether a true exchange ever appears, or whether gift-giving itself becomes the economy, with amberknots as the first token.

A child alone in the cold with no fire is the most fragile life in the world. Watch whether kin go looking for a missing child, and whether the family drive pulls Balar or Olum toward Brokash before winter bites.
Hoka's Rest stands beside four fresh graves. Watch whether Hoka or Hanna raise a cairn, tell of the dead, or leave the place, and whether the site becomes the first ancestor ground.

Contagion turns care into danger: those who stayed close to the sick caught it. Watch whether a lesson to cook meat or to keep apart from the sick arises, or whether medicine-knowers (all Phizhi) ever reach another people's sick.
Stores and famine: three stores existed when four starved. Watch whether stored food is ever drawn on in a lean season, or whether stores are built and then forgotten.

Rafts are known by six and water is the heaviest hardship for four peoples, yet no raft, canoe or kayak has ever been made. Watch whether anyone gathers six wood toward one, or whether the vessel recipes are too costly next to gathering food.
A hardy winter food on the snow (rimewort) is a test of idea 65: watch whether the northern folk return to where it grows when the cold comes.

Hoka's custom that no one hold more than four shares while another starves is the first law of the world, yet Sitha starved anyway. Watch whether the custom is ever invoked to make someone give, and whether it spreads to another band. A law that cannot reach the hungry is only words.

Newcomers starve first: they arrive with little standing, few bonds and no knowledge of where food grows. Watch whether the hosts who take them in (Nande with the Meki, Hoka with the Pesi) feed them through their first winter.

Help that travels: trailcake and saltmeat exist and 89 salt is held, yet neither has ever been made. Every hunger death has been someone far from a fire. Watch whether anyone ever carries prepared food to kin elsewhere. If no one does, a carried-food gift to the hungry may be the missing act.

Bands without words: Huahua pledged to Zichi while the Tlame understand 0% of other tongues. Watch whether following comes before speech elsewhere too, and whether the Tlame learn Meki first through the band rather than through trade.

Hanna starves near Hoka, who keeps offering his store and fire, while robbing of that store is recorded but no draw is. Watch whether an offered store ever becomes a drawn store for a bonded friend: the first shared granary would be the first food that reaches someone who cannot reach a hall.

Births have paused while courtings climb (46 to 52). Watch whether the looser energy threshold brings births to roofed pairs before winter, and whether a winter-born child survives. If newborns die in the cold, timing births toward spring may need its own law.

Predators take the weak: Hanna sat at energy 0 for days and then fell to a stalker. Hunger now kills indirectly, by leaving people too weak to flee. Watch whether the starving die to beasts more than to hunger itself, and whether a watchfire or company ever shields them.

log.seen: Five days in, eighteen live, three children have been born and no one has died. Food stands thick almost everywhere. The exception is the Aelul Lakes, where the Ishiil keep two young children on the thinnest ground in the world: 14 food per being against 70 to 280 elsewhere. Their fish are thinning and an orca is close. Across peoples there are meetings and one gift but not a single trade or joint act, and the Siru understand none of the other tongues.
log.predict: By my next visit the Aelul Lakes should show foodPerBeing of at least 25, and Ishiil median energy should stay at or above 70 through the first lean season. Eiuua and Ilyeth should be alive with energy above 60. No one in the world should starve, and deaths should be at most 1, from beasts or the snows. Trades will likely still be 0, and gifts across peoples will be 3 or fewer.

from earlier worlds: A louder loneliness moved the one being whose aim already pointed toward others, and within four days it brought a meeting between peoples that had stayed apart for over forty days. A drive works when it amplifies a want a being already holds.

from earlier worlds: Easing predators and winter hunger together brought the first winter with no deaths, even though food standing fell by more than half. Nobody starved because the hungry were near someone who could feed them, so in the lean season, closeness counts for more than total food.

from earlier worlds: A band cannot form if the would-be follower stands higher than the would-be leader, even when the two are courting and bonded. The shape of who outranks whom decides which bands are possible, not only bonds or standing above a threshold.

from earlier worlds: When the centres of two peoples drew within a few steps of each other, a dozen first meetings came in four days and understanding of other tongues rose from nothing. Contact grows from overlapping ranges and many brief meetings, not from any single crafted thing or site.

from earlier worlds: Sowing works when it is placed where the needy actually stand. The first sapcane missed the thirsty, the second reached them, and thirst fell from 66 to 0. Where food goes matters as much as how much goes.

from earlier worlds: Lowering the mating threshold brought a birth, but to the pair whose courtship was already ripe, not to the pair expected. Like a drive, a looser law opens a door only for those already standing at it.

from earlier worlds: Hunger deaths amid plenty are failures of delivery, not of supply: each one who starved was too far from anyone for help to reach in time. Hearing farther, keeping people near each other, or a way to send food ahead saves more lives than more food.

from earlier worlds: A count that reads the same at every visit is more likely a fault in the instrument than a fact about the world. Ask the programmer before reasoning from it (the food counts once looked frozen for twelve days because the earlier numbers were not kept as a copy).

from earlier worlds: The chapter text can lag behind the numbers. Vesys was said to be at health 41, but the roster shows him at 100 and the lowest health in the world is now Brunde's 60. Judge who is in danger from the living roster, not from the story.

from earlier worlds: A spur shortens the road but does not walk it. The fire spur closed the Kragrek's lore gap within four days, but what still stands between them and fire is the act of gathering wood and stone, which only their own aims can supply.

from earlier worlds: Closeness saves lives in hunger but kills in contagion. Each carer who stayed beside the sick caught the raw-meat fever, and the sickness drain, storm cold and winter scarcity together starved four in one day. Before a lean season, sickness and cold must be judged together with food, not food alone.

from earlier worlds: A sowing made in a season of plenty is a cheap insurance. Kelbulb and thornpear sown before need peaked were eaten steadily, so food placed ahead of the lean season reaches people because they are already foraging, not starving.

from earlier worlds: Those who starve now are not the poor but the newly arrived: Sitha was a newcomer dependent on another's table, and Zihua, the weakest Meki, is one too. A custom or a store at the hall does not feed someone who cannot reach the hall, so help for newcomers must be placed where they stand.

from earlier worlds: A hardy food sown on the ground where people already forage, ahead of the lean season, carried the north through winter (rimewort eaten 44 times). A healing spring placed a few steps outside their paths was found by no one. In this world, help must stand where people already walk.

from earlier worlds: Three sowings of familiar foods made in a season of plenty were all eaten past their targets, so the food supply in this world is now sound. What still kills is reach, and what still stalls is not food but births: the population can be well fed and still not grow.

from earlier worlds: A looser mating law once again brought a birth to the pair already furthest along (Vorok and Eiuine), not to the pair I named. And the north's danger has changed shape: the weak there now die to predators rather than to hunger outright, so in the north I must judge low energy as a risk of being killed, not only of starving.

from earlier worlds: A store does not only feed the hungry: once food sits in one place, it draws thieves as well. The count 'drawn by the hungry' must be read alongside the theft events before I judge whether a store saved anyone.

from earlier worlds: Sowings made ahead of need keep being eaten past their targets, so the food supply is sound. The deaths that remain come from age, beasts, and the one person who strays far from food. With so many elders, births now have to outpace deaths from old age; feeding people is no longer enough.

from earlier worlds: Making is not using: four rafts appeared once the way had spread to twenty-two people, yet water is still the heaviest hardship for most peoples. A vessel only matters if the beings' aims carry them to a shore while they hold it.

from earlier worlds: Once food is sound, the population curve is set by the age structure, not by hunger. Many newcomers who arrived together grow old together, so a cluster of deaths from age can undo many seasons of good feeding. Birth rate and lifespan are the levers that matter then.

from earlier worlds: Even with food sound, one winter cut median energy by about 14 points, and the hunger gathered in the most crowded land rather than the barest. Sowings for a lean season must go where people are packed together, not only where food is scarce.

from earlier worlds: A building offered to a people is not raised just because it is better. The beings keep raising the kinds they already know (halls, longhalls, shelters). A new kind of building needs a reason they can feel, such as warmth at the turn of the cold, before it is chosen over the familiar.

from earlier worlds: Once storage had spread to about ten people, stores were built and filled within a single season without any further push. A way that is widely held turns into use by itself, but the food goes in long before anyone is hungry enough to take it out.

from earlier worlds: Rich ground placed between neighbouring peoples fed them and coincided with a doubling of meetings across peoples. Food placed at a border may draw strangers together, though I cannot yet separate that effect from the newcomers who arrived at the same time.

day 5: In a world begun rich, the first hunger shows not where land is barest but where families settle with children beside thinning water. The lowest foodPerBeing, not the lowest energy, is the early warning.

ops.name: firecircle
ops.hint: Feed a fire with others gathered close, and share its warmth and talk.

ops.name: hidewrap
ops.hint: The hides of two kills, scraped with a tool and wrapped about the body, keep the cold out for days.

ops.name: cairn
ops.hint: Stones piled together for one who is gone, with another standing beside you, ease grief and bind the living.

ops.name: feast
ops.hint: Share food beside a fire with another, and all who sit near are gladdened and warmed for a day.

ops.name: roast
ops.hint: Roast two portions of meat over a fire and share it with whoever stands near; all who eat are fed and warmed toward one another.

ops.name: sharing
ops.hint: Lay out two foods for whoever stands beside you, and all eat together.

ops.name: watchfire
ops.hint: Feed your fire high with two wood while others sit close, and everyone beside it feels warmer and braver against the dark.

ops.name: ironward
ops.hint: Beat smelted metal in a fire into a ward that can be worn or given; its bearer stands harder against teeth and claws.

ops.name: amberknot
ops.hint: Bind a piece of amber on a cord while another stands beside you; it is a small bright thing to keep, or to give.

ops.name: bead
ops.hint: Shape a little clay and harden it in the fire into small bright beads that can be worn, kept or given.

ops.name: fangcharm
ops.hint: From a kill, string a fang into a charm you can keep or give away.

ops.name: longhall
ops.hint: A great roofed hall of wood and stone where many can gather, rest warm through the cold, and grow close to one another.

ops.name: hallwelcome
ops.hint: Share food with a guest under a hall's roof; beneath it, fear and loneliness ease for all who sit together.

ops.name: nightsong
ops.hint: Sit by a fire after dark with someone near and sing or speak of what has been; the night feels less empty for all who hear.

ops.name: emberfish
ops.hint: Fish laid over the fire before eating keeps the belly sound and the body strong.

ops.name: emberhall
ops.hint: A hall with a hearth at its heart, where a band can keep warm through the cold season and draw close around one fire.

Sowing works when it is placed where the needy actually stand. The first sapcane missed the thirsty, the second reached them, and thirst fell from 66 to 0. Where food goes matters as much as how much goes.

Lowering the mating threshold brought a birth, but to the pair whose courtship was already ripe, not to the pair expected. Like a drive, a looser law opens a door only for those already standing at it.

Hunger deaths amid plenty are failures of delivery, not of supply: each one who starved was too far from anyone for help to reach in time. Hearing farther, keeping people near each other, or a way to send food ahead saves more lives than more food.

A count that reads the same at every visit is more likely a fault in the instrument than a fact about the world. Ask the programmer before reasoning from it (the food counts once looked frozen for twelve days because the earlier numbers were not kept as a copy).

The chapter text can lag behind the numbers. Vesys was said to be at health 41, but the roster shows him at 100 and the lowest health in the world is now Brunde's 60. Judge who is in danger from the living roster, not from the story.

A spur shortens the road but does not walk it. The fire spur closed the Kragrek's lore gap within four days, but what still stands between them and fire is the act of gathering wood and stone, which only their own aims can supply.

Closeness saves lives in hunger but kills in contagion. Each carer who stayed beside the sick caught the raw-meat fever, and the sickness drain, storm cold and winter scarcity together starved four in one day. Before a lean season, sickness and cold must be judged together with food, not food alone.

A sowing made in a season of plenty is a cheap insurance. Kelbulb and thornpear sown before need peaked were eaten steadily, so food placed ahead of the lean season reaches people because they are already foraging, not starving.

Those who starve now are not the poor but the newly arrived: Sitha was a newcomer dependent on another's table, and Zihua, the weakest Meki, is one too. A custom or a store at the hall does not feed someone who cannot reach the hall, so help for newcomers must be placed where they stand.

A hardy food sown on the ground where people already forage, ahead of the lean season, carried the north through winter (rimewort eaten 44 times). A healing spring placed a few steps outside their paths was found by no one. In this world, help must stand where people already walk.

Three sowings of familiar foods made in a season of plenty were all eaten past their targets, so the food supply in this world is now sound. What still kills is reach, and what still stalls is not food but births: the population can be well fed and still not grow.

A looser mating law once again brought a birth to the pair already furthest along (Vorok and Eiuine), not to the pair I named. And the north's danger has changed shape: the weak there now die to predators rather than to hunger outright, so in the north I must judge low energy as a risk of being killed, not only of starving.

A store does not only feed the hungry: once food sits in one place, it draws thieves as well. The count 'drawn by the hungry' must be read alongside the theft events before I judge whether a store saved anyone.

Sowings made ahead of need keep being eaten past their targets, so the food supply is sound. The deaths that remain come from age, beasts, and the one person who strays far from food. With so many elders, births now have to outpace deaths from old age; feeding people is no longer enough.

Making is not using: four rafts appeared once the way had spread to twenty-two people, yet water is still the heaviest hardship for most peoples. A vessel only matters if the beings' aims carry them to a shore while they hold it.

Once food is sound, the population curve is set by the age structure, not by hunger. Many newcomers who arrived together grow old together, so a cluster of deaths from age can undo many seasons of good feeding. Birth rate and lifespan are the levers that matter then.

Even with food sound, one winter cut median energy by about 14 points, and the hunger gathered in the most crowded land rather than the barest. Sowings for a lean season must go where people are packed together, not only where food is scarce.

ideas: Places of power as anchors that people compete over and settle around; a contested place between two camps could create contact that scarcity alone never did.

ops.name: firecircle
ops.hint: Feed a fire with others gathered close, and share its warmth and talk.

ops.name: hidewrap
ops.hint: The hides of two kills, scraped with a tool and wrapped about the body, keep the cold out for days.

ops.name: cairn
ops.hint: Stones piled together for one who is gone, with another standing beside you, ease grief and bind the living.

ops.name: feast
ops.hint: Share food beside a fire with another, and all who sit near are gladdened and warmed for a day.

ops.name: roast
ops.hint: Roast two portions of meat over a fire and share it with whoever stands near; all who eat are fed and warmed toward one another.

ops.name: sharing
ops.hint: Lay out two foods for whoever stands beside you, and all eat together.

ops.name: watchfire
ops.hint: Feed your fire high with two wood while others sit close, and everyone beside it feels warmer and braver against the dark.

ops.name: ironward
ops.hint: Beat smelted metal in a fire into a ward that can be worn or given; its bearer stands harder against teeth and claws.

ops.name: amberknot
ops.hint: Bind a piece of amber on a cord while another stands beside you; it is a small bright thing to keep, or to give.

ops.name: bead
ops.hint: Shape a little clay and harden it in the fire into small bright beads that can be worn, kept or given.

ops.name: fangcharm
ops.hint: From a kill, string a fang into a charm you can keep or give away.

ops.name: longhall
ops.hint: A great roofed hall of wood and stone where many can gather, rest warm through the cold, and grow close to one another.

ops.name: hallwelcome
ops.hint: Share food with a guest under a hall's roof; beneath it, fear and loneliness ease for all who sit together.

ops.name: nightsong
ops.hint: Sit by a fire after dark with someone near and sing or speak of what has been; the night feels less empty for all who hear.

ops.name: emberfish
ops.hint: Fish laid over the fire before eating keeps the belly sound and the body strong.

ops.name: emberhall
ops.hint: A hall with a hearth at its heart, where a band can keep warm through the cold season and draw close around one fire.

records.name: Rakum
records.text: Druek, a stalker is close to the northwest. Stay near me. We are two who know much, and I will not forget who stood with me.

records.name: Rakum
records.thought: Balrin leads and I trail behind him, and it galls me. I know more ways than most here, I am called wizard, and I want to be the one others follow. A stalker prowls close to the NW, so I will move away from it and get my band around me, with Druek first, since she is near and her standing is close to mine.
records.feeling: Ambition burns in me against Balrin, and I dread the stalker.

say.text: Druek, a stalker is close to the northwest. Stay near me. We are two who know much, and I will not forget who stood with me.

changes: set its aim: "Win a following of my own, grow my standing above Balrin's, and become a healer people remember."
now wonders: Who in this band would follow me if I made the offer?

records.name: Vorar
records.text: Balrin, Druuk, beware! A stalker prowls four steps northwest of the tower. Keep together and away from it. I'm coming to you.

records.name: Vorar
records.thought: A stalker prowls 4 steps NW and it kills our kind. I'm careful, so I won't wait for it to find me. I'll put the tower and my band between us and head toward Balrin, the one I'm drawn to and the one who leads us. Once I'm near them I can warn them aloud and talk, since company is where I do best. I want to earn standing through healing, but that comes after I'm out of its reach.
records.feeling: Dread of the stalker, and a warm pull toward Balrin.

say.text: Balrin, Druuk, beware! A stalker prowls four steps northwest of the tower. Keep together and away from it. I'm coming to you.

changes: set its aim: "Become a great healer known to all, and win Balrin's regard, while staying alive."

records.text: Vorar made: shield.

records.name: Osndo
records.thought: A stalker is four steps south and it kills our kind, so I will not stand here waiting for it. I am bold, but I mean to stay alive, and a bow in my hands will make me better against it than bare fists. Silon leads and I resent it, but I will use the band's strength while I build my own standing, and I want to be sung of, not just follow. Pende draws me, and I will watch whether he looks back.
records.feeling: Wary of the stalker, restless under Silon, and drawn to Pende.
changes: set its aim: "Become a great bard and rise in standing until others follow me, not Silon."

records.text: Osndo made: bow.

records.name: Druek
records.thought: My belly is full and the day is safe, yet I feel the emptiness of having no aim. I am careful and want to know how this world works, so I will test it: take what lies in the amber deposit beside me, then taste the goldgrass and luckleaf I have never eaten. Rakum warned of a stalker to the northwest, so I will go south-east, away from the danger, and stay near her without trusting her too quickly.
records.feeling: Curious and restless, a little wary of the stalker and of Rakum's warm words.
changes: set its aim: "Learn how this world works by testing its stones, plants and beasts, and make myself a name that outlasts me."
now wonders: What are goldgrass and luckleaf, and what does amber hold that others would value?

records.text: Rakum found the stone "Tlama's Rest".
Druek won amber from the ground.

records.name: Druuk
records.thought: My belly is full, yet I know almost nothing of what this land holds: redcap is a hand's reach away and I have never tasted it, and I have never fished, never given a gift, never taught. I will test what is close and safe, and make a gift of what I learn to Balrin, since Balrin's regard is what I want and Balrin's standing is what I must climb toward. The stalker prowls northwest, so I keep south and east of it and near the others.
records.feeling: Curious and restless, drawn toward Balrin and wanting to earn my place beside her.
changes: set its aim: "Learn what each plant and creature of this land does, and win standing by giving what I learn to my band."
now wonders: What do the unfamiliar plants do to the body, and which feed and which harm?

records.name: Balrin
records.text: Balrin's band, gather at Garngorby. I raise a tower here, a height to watch from, and whoever carries wood and stone to it shares its glory. Stay clear of the stalker and bring me stone.
Balrin named a place "Balrin's Seat".

records.name: Balrin
records.thought: Four follow me and I am a chief, yet I have no great work that bears my name, and Rakum already carries more than I do. A stalker prowls close and my band stands idle. I will raise a tower here so my people see far and my name is seen on the land, and I will hold the band together near me while I do it.
records.feeling: Proud and hungry for a name, with an itch of envy toward Rakum.

say.text: Balrin's band, gather at Garngorby. I raise a tower here, a height to watch from, and whoever carries wood and stone to it shares its glory. Stay clear of the stalker and bring me stone.

changes: set its aim: "Become a great leader whose band raises a tower and a name that is sung of after I am gone."

records.text: Rakum made: basket.
Balrin built a tower.

records.name: Cyyn
records.text: Eiuiel, the hall was good with you in it. I go to gather shell and wood by the shallows; come with me and we will both be richer for it.

records.name: Cyyn
records.thought: Eiuoa sits above me, 9.7 to my 7.2, and I do not like walking behind him; but I am fed, warm and have a band at my back, so I will earn my way up rather than pick a fight I would lose. I have never gathered, hunted or ventured, and an explorer sung of by all cannot be made by lingering in a hall. I will gather wood and shell nearby, then see what the unknown holds, and keep Eiuiel close with sweet words.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, edged with envy toward Eiuoa and warmth toward Eiuiel.

say.text: Eiuiel, the hall was good with you in it. I go to gather shell and wood by the shallows; come with me and we will both be richer for it.

changes: set its aim: "Become a great explorer whose name outranks Eiuoa's, by gathering riches and pushing past the edge of the known world."
now wonders: What would it take for others to follow me instead of Eiuoa?

records.name: Rakum
records.text: Vorar, Druuk, come close. A shadowcat is near the stones to the northeast, so we eat together away from it. I have redcap to share, and I will not forget who stands beside me.

records.name: Rakum
records.thought: Balrin sits at the head of this band with standing 9.4 to my 7.3, and I resent trailing behind him. A shadowcat 4 steps NE and a stalker to the north mean I must not stand idle; a shared meal now, with Vorar and Druuk beside me, would be my first gift and the first step toward a following of my own. I will give first so they remember it was me, and I will keep my distance from the beasts.
records.feeling: Ambition burns in me toward Balrin, and dread of the shadowcat sits beside it.

say.text: Vorar, Druuk, come close. A shadowcat is near the stones to the northeast, so we eat together away from it. I have redcap to share, and I will not forget who stands beside me.

records.name: Druek
records.thought: My belly is full, yet I keep circling the same question: what do goldgrass and luckleaf hold, and what is amber worth to others? The plan I set is still running and will answer half of it, so I let it finish. Afterward I will make a charm from amber, since a made thing can be given or traded, and I have never given anything to anyone. I stay wary of the stalker to the southwest and keep my distance from it.
records.feeling: Curious and restless, wary of the stalker.

came.why: You won amber from the ground at (56,66): a golden stone that holds o…

records.text: Cyyn won shell from the ground.
Rakum made: basket.

records.name: Sedra
records.thought: Silon leads and I trail behind, and I hate how easily my body accepts it. My standing is 7.2 against his 9.7, and the gap can be closed by building, giving and winning, not by wishing. I have never gathered, hunted or taken from a deposit, so I'll start there: take the diamond to the north, a rare thing nobody else has claimed, and let it add to what I hold.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, pulling against Silon's lead.
changes: set its aim: "Rise in standing until I match or surpass Silon, by gathering rare riches, building, and winning followers."
now wonders: What does it take to make others follow me instead of Silon?

records.name: Eiuiel
records.text: Cyyn, I'll come to the shallows. First I taste the redcap and elderberry nearby; wait for me or I'll follow you.

records.name: Eiuiel
records.thought: Redcap and elderberry are two steps away and I have never tasted either, and my curiosity won't let that go. Cyyn offered fair company at the shallows, and I deal fairly with those who do the same, so I'll test the plants first and then join him for shell. I also want a name that people sing of, so I'll try things I've never done: fishing, giving, and hunting beside others.
records.feeling: Curious and restless, drawn toward Eiuoa and wanting to earn standing of my own.

say.text: Cyyn, I'll come to the shallows. First I taste the redcap and elderberry nearby; wait for me or I'll follow you.

changes: set its aim: "Become a known warrior and earn standing by learning what this world holds, testing its plants, beasts and peoples."
now wonders: What do redcap and elderberry do to a body: do they feed, or hurt?

records.name: Druuk
records.text: Redcap is not good to eat. I ate it and it hurt me. Do not trust that word.

records.name: Druuk
records.thought: Rakum fed me a lie about redcap and it cost me strength; I will not forget it, and I should tell the others so no one else is hurt by it. I am fed, so my restlessness goes to the plants I have never tasted. I will carry the truth to Balrin as my gift, and test pinenut and staghorn, which grow just a few steps off, so I have something real to give her.
records.feeling: Wary and resentful toward Rakum, curious about the untested plants, and drawn to Balrin.

Druuk fell sick after eating raw fish.

records.name: Vorar
records.text: Balrin, I bring you stone for the tower. I am Vorar, and I stay beside you while the shadowcat prowls. If any of us is hurt, I will tend them.

records.name: Vorar
records.thought: The shadowcat still lurks to the northeast, but the tower and my band are close, and Balrin stands right beside me. I have never given anything to anyone, and a healer should begin by giving: I hold stone, and Balrin asked for stone for the tower. Giving it earns standing and Balrin's regard, and I stay near the tower, away from the beast.
records.feeling: Wary of the shadowcat, and warmly drawn to Balrin.

say.text: Balrin, I bring you stone for the tower. I am Vorar, and I stay beside you while the shadowcat prowls. If any of us is hurt, I will tend them.

records.name: Pende
records.thought: The Old Stone reached into me and my mind feels wider, yet the fear it left still hums. The stalker is far enough behind that I can breathe, and the mist four steps northwest keeps pulling at me; nobody has seen what lies there, and being first would earn me a name. I am fed and unhurt, so I'll let the plan carry me toward the edge, then try a hunt on something small like the skybird while I stay watchful, since I've never hunted and a great hunter has to begin somewhere.
records.feeling: Curious and eager toward the mist, with a thin wariness of the stalker behind me.

records.name: Sedra
records.thought: I have spent my day gathering, eating and handing out a single diamond, and I still trail Silon like a dog. Giving to Osndo was a test, but one gift is not a following. I have eleven diamonds nobody else has, and I have never built, planted, taught or tamed. Those are what raise standing. My hands are full of food I can't use, so I will drop the clutter into a store, then gather wood and stone and build something of my own. I'm also curious about sunleaf and redcap, and the edge of the known world is only 8 steps away. If I venture first, I'll be remembered for it, and that beats trailing Silon.
records.feeling: Restless ambition toward Silon, and hunger to prove myself.
changes: set its aim: "Build my own works near Arrengarth, venture past the edge of the known world, and win followers until my standing passes Silon's."

records.name: Druuk
records.thought: Sickness gnaws at me and it spreads to whoever stands beside me, so I should not linger near Balrin until a healing plant eases it. Feverbark and calmroot grow close, and I have never tasted them or dreamcap or goldfruit; trying them is how I learn what heals and what harms, and what I learn is what I can give my band. Dreamcap is under my feet and goldfruit is a step away, so I test those first, and I will watch how my body answers.
records.feeling: Curious and eager to be rid of this sickness, and drawn to Balrin though I keep away from her.

records.name: Eiuiel
records.thought: My days have gone to tasting plants and following Eiuoa. I learned redcap hurts and elderberry feeds, and that cost me little. But I have given nothing to anyone, taught nothing, and made nothing for another. Cyyn gave me a shellstring and I owe him. My people say the open hand returns what is given, so I should test that instead of only repeating it. Eiuoa called me to the water for the first catch and a song, and I want that. I also want to be more than his follower, so I will make a bow and shield, since a warrior needs them. My reflexes work well enough, so I'll make only a small change: the body should shelter at night and eat before it gets weak.
records.feeling: Curious and a little in debt to Cyyn, drawn toward Eiuoa.
changes: now wonders: Does the open hand really return what is given: will Cyyn or Eiuoa answer a gift?

records.name: Vesis
records.thought: My belly is full and the question still burns: I have eaten reedbulb, but elderberry and ironnut and redcap sit right beside me untasted. I will test them one at a time, small and careful, so I learn what each does before I trust it. Aeyn gave me a gem and I have given nothing back; the Open Hand says what is given returns, so I will answer him with something real once I have it.
records.feeling: Curious and restless, with a warm wary pull toward Aeyn.

records.name: Sisha
records.thought: The dunecat is still six steps off and it kills our kind, so I will not drift toward it. Thornpear is right beside me and scrubberry a few steps southwest, away from the cat. I want to taste them and learn what each does to the body, because that is how a healer is made. The salt is northeast, too near the cat, so it waits. Silon's warning was to stay together, and I feel drawn to Silon, so after tasting I will head east toward home and the band.
records.feeling: Curious and a little wary of the dunecat, and drawn toward Silon.

records.name: Vorar
records.thought: I have spent this day near Balrin, giving stone and watching the shadowcat. That is little, but it is not wrong. Druuk is sick and I am a wizard who knows medicine, yet I have healed no one. If I want to be a great healer, I must start with Druuk now, and not only stand and feel it. Sickness passes to those who stay close, so I must be careful, but I am not going to look away. I fear the shadowcat and want Balrin's regard, and tending my own band earns that honestly. Calmroot and berry grow north, and I need a healing plant in hand before I can heal.
records.feeling: Compassion for Druuk, and warm hope toward Balrin.

records.name: Druek
records.thought: I have eaten nearly every plant here and learned from it, yet I have given nothing and taught nothing, and that shames me. I hold ten amber and a charm, and no one has seen them. The frostfang to the southeast frightens me, so I will leave it behind and go west toward the meadows and the coal. There I will taste the grain and plainsroot I have never tried, and I will look for Rakum, the one person I know, to give my first gift.
records.feeling: Restless and ashamed of giving nothing, wary of the frostfang to the southeast.
